title: One owner group's homes: cash at the end of 2024, IOUs at the end of 2025
question: Which nursing-home groups saw cash fall and related-party balances rise in 2025?
finding: Yes, one group stands out. The 27 California homes whose 2025 reports name Life Generations Healthcare / Generations Healthcare, Inc as parent (8 in the Bay Area, 1 in San Francisco) had $314.0 million of cash and securities at the end of 2024 and $6.1 million at the end of 2025 in the State’s pivot profiles. The profiles use a derived cash column. The corresponding figures on the 27 Life Generations homes’ submitted balance sheets (page 5.1, lines 5 and 10) were $314,215,627 and $6,598,810. Over the same year the net amount related parties owed them went from -$36.3 million to $298.8 million, while the homes reported $53.6 million of net income. No other parent with two or more homes shows the same pattern (cash down $10 million or more and the related balance up by at least three quarters of that).
how: Homes with a 2024 and a 2025 report, grouped by the parent organisation named in the 2025 report (page 3.1); the two spellings of one parent's name are joined. Cash and securities from the 2024 and 2025 pivot profiles; net amount owed by related parties from the complete data sets (the case's definition). Groups listed when their cash fell by $10 million or more and the related-party balance rose by at least three quarters of that fall.
limits: Pooling cash in a parent's account is permitted and common; the homes still report the money as theirs, now as an amount owed by the parent. Common explanations include a new central treasury or a loan agreement that requires cash to be held centrally. The 2025 reports are as submitted, not audited, and a change in how the same cash is classified would show the same pattern. Only the parent's own accounts, which are not public, would show where the money is.
